verdict.rationale: Pipecat is a framework for building real-time voice and multimodal agents. Its closest support for background work is handing long-running tools and complex tasks off to subagents, plus multi-agent systems that fan out in parallel and coordinate across processes. Telephony sessions can also start from a carrier webhook rather than a user's client request. That is only glancing support for user-configured background automations: missing for 10: scheduled or recurring job triggers, a documented way to set up and run unattended background automations outside a live conversation, and independent or hands-on corroboration of autonomous background operation.
